'''Tarence Anthony Kinsey''' (born March 21, 1984) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played for the [[Memphis Grizzlies]]
and the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]]. He also played for several teams in [[Europe]]. He played [[college basketball]] for [[South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball|University of South Carolina]].

==College career==
Kinsey attended and played [[college basketball|collegiately]] at the [[University of South Carolina]] where he helped lead the Gamecocks to two straight NIT championships; averaging 19.4 points, 4.2 rebounds, 3.2 assists, 2.6 steals and shooting 53% from the field in the NIT Tournament.

===NIT Championship Game 2005===
While a junior at the University of South Carolina, Kinsey was an essential player on the Gamecocks basketball team. As the team made it to the NIT (National Invitation Tournament), they reached the championship game against [[St. Joseph's University]]. With less than 6 seconds remaining on the clock, St. Joe's sharpshooter [[Pat Carroll (basketball)|Pat Carroll]] hit a 3-pointer to tie the game up, 57–57. Kinsey got the inbounds pass for USC, dribbled up court, and fired a 3-pointer that hit nothing but net with 1.3 seconds left to win the NIT for South Carolina, 60–57.

==Professional career==
===Memphis Grizzlies (2006–2008)===
Undrafted out of college, Kinsey played the [[2006–07 NBA season]] for the [[Memphis Grizzlies]], averaging 7.7 points in 48 games. He started 12 games for the Grizzlies, averaging 18.8 points, 4.4 rebounds and 2.1 assists per game.

Kinsey took part in the [[2007 NBA Europe Live Tour]] in Spain. He started the [[2007–08 NBA season]] for the Memphis Grizzlies and played in 11 games for Memphis this season, averaging 3.6 points and 1.1 rebounds in limited action.

===Fenerbahçe Ülker (2008)===
After being released by the Grizzlies, Kinsey signed a contract to play in the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi|TBL]] for the [[Fenerbahçe Men's Basketball|Fenerbahçe Ülker]] in Turkey.<ref>{{cite news|title=Fener signs guard Tarence Kinsey|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/21930/fener-signs-guard-tarence-kinsey|access-date=July 23, 2015|work=Euroleague.net|date=January 5, 2008}}</ref> He averaged 9.2 points in 14 regular season games with Fenerbahce Ulker and helped the club to win the Beko Basketball League Finals (the final stage of the Turkish Basketball League playoffs).

Kinsey posted averages of 8.8 points on .492 shooting and 2.8 rebounds in 12 Euroleague games helping Fenerbahçe Ülker reach the quarterfinals of [[2007–08 Euroleague]]. Kinsey tied for team high in scoring with 12 points in the first game of the best of three game quarterfinal series against [[Mens Sana Basket|Montepaschi Siena]].

===Cleveland Cavaliers (2008–2009)===
On August 1, 2008, Kinsey signed a one-year contract with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Cavaliers sign former Grizzlies guard Kinsey | date=August 4, 2008 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3518966 |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=September 10, 2013}}</ref>

In the early part of the season, Kinsey usually only played during [[garbage time]]. After injuries to starting [[shooting guard]] [[Delonte West]] and top reserve [[Aleksandar Pavlović (basketball)|Sasha Pavlović]], Kinsey began playing more and even started a few games and played well until spraining his ankle in a game against [[Orlando Magic|Orlando]]. Kinsey returned following the [[2009 NBA All-Star Game|All-Star game]], and once again was the third-string shooting guard as West and Pavlović returned from injury.

===Return to Fenerbahçe (2009–2011)===
On August 25, 2009, Kinsey returned to [[Fenerbahçe Men's Basketball|Fenerbahçe Ülker]] for a second stint, signing a two-year deal.<ref>{{cite news|title=Fenerbahce brings back Tarence Kinsey|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/57883/fenerbahce-brings-back-tarence-kinsey|access-date=July 22, 2015|work=Euroleague.net|date=August 25, 2009}}</ref>

===Anadolu Efes (2011–2012)===
In July 2011, he signed a one-year deal with [[Anadolu Efes S.K.|Anadolu Efes]].<ref>{{cite web|title=ANADOLU EFES lands Kinsey |url=http://www.euroleague.net/euroleaguenews/transactions/2011-12-signings/i/86886/5611/anadolu-efes-lands-swingman-kinsey |work=Euroleague.net |access-date=July 22, 2015 |date=July 26, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121019155753/http://www.euroleague.net/euroleaguenews/transactions/2011-12-signings/i/86886/5611/anadolu-efes-lands-swingman-kinsey |archive-date=October 19, 2012 }}</ref>

===Pesaro / Unicaja Malaga (2012–2013)===
On September 26, 2012, Kinsey signed with the [[Golden State Warriors]] of the NBA.<ref>[https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors_sign_four_free_agents Warriors Sign Four Free Agents]</ref> However, he did not make the team's final roster.<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20130130011656/http://www.nba.com/warriors/node/61162|title=Warriors Waive Brown, Goulbourne, Jackson and Kinsey}}</ref> On December 14, 2012, Kinsey signed with [[Victoria Libertas Pesaro]] in Italy's [[Lega Basket Serie A]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Scavolini Banca Marche Pesaro announced Tarence Kinsey|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/italy/serie-a/47832/scavolini-banca-marche-pesaro-announced-tarence-kinsey.html|work=Sportando.net|access-date=April 19, 2013}}</ref> On April 19, 2013, he left Pesaro and signed with [[Baloncesto Málaga|Unicaja Málaga]] of Spain for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Unicaja Malaga signs Tarence Kinsey|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/spain/54396/unicaja-malaga-signs-tarence-kinsey.html|work=Sportando.net|access-date=April 19, 2013}}</ref>

===Partizan Belgrade (2013–2014)===
On September 9, 2013, Kinsey signed a one-year deal with the Serbian team [[KK Partizan|Partizan Belgrade]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Terens Kinsi novi je igrač Partizana! |url=http://www.kkpartizan.rs/sr/vest.php?id=1355 |publisher=kkpartizan.rs |language=sr |access-date=September 9, 2013 |url-status=dead December, his block on [[Fenerbahçe Men's Basketball|Fenerbahçe]]'s [[Bojan Bogdanović|Bogdanović]] was a top play.<ref>{{cite web|title=Kinsey's huge block on Bogdanovic leads Euroleague Top 10 Plays|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/cups/euroleague/69584/kinsey-s-huge-block-on-bogdanovic-leads-euroleague-top-10-plays.html|work=Sportando|access-date=February 1, 2014}}</ref> In the [[2013–14 seasons of his career, averaging career-high 14.8 points, 4.6 rebounds, over 16 games in the [[2013–14 Euroleague|Euroleague]].

===Nizhny Novgorod (2014–2015)===
On August 4, 2014, he signed a one-year deal with the Russian team [[BC Nizhny Novgorod|Nizhny Novgorod]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Nizhny Novgorod adds veteran swingman Kinsey|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/140003/nizhny-novgorod-adds-veteran-swingman-kinsey|access-date=July 22, 2015|work=Euroleague.net|date=August 4, 2014}}</ref> Nizhny Novgorod ended the competition in the [[2014–15 VTB United League|VTB United League]] after being eliminated by [[PBC CSKA Moscow|CSKA Moscow]] with 3–0 in the semifinal series.

===Trabzonspor (2015)===
On July 22, 2015, Kinsey signed a one-year deal with the Turkish club [[Trabzonspor B.K.|Trabzonspor]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Trabzonspor brings Kinsey back to Turkey|url=http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/67vs4qkw9eghjl77|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150723052518/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/67vs4qkw9eghjl77|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 23, 2015|access-date=July 22, 2015|work=Eurocupbasketball.com|date=July 22, 2015}}</ref> On December 27, 2015, he parted ways with Trabzonspor after appearing in eleven [[2015–16 Turkish Basketball Super League|league]] games and ten [[2015–16 Eurocup Basketball|EuroCup]] games.<ref>{{cite news|title=Tarence Kinsey, Trabzonspor agreed to part ways|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/186069/tarence-kinsey-trabzonspor-agreed-to-part-ways.html|access-date=December 28, 2015|work=Sportando.com|date=December 27, 2015}}</ref>

===Crvena zvezda (2015–2016)===
On December 28, 2015, Kinsey signed with the Serbian club [[KK Crvena zvezda|Crvena zvezda]] for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Terens Kinzi u Crvenoj zvezdi!|url=http://www.kkcrvenazvezda.rs/terens-kinzi-u-crvenoj-zvezdi-28-12-2015.html|access-date=December 28, 2015|work=kkcrvenazvezda.rs|date=December 28, 2015|language=sr|archive-date=March 31, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180331040343/http://www.kkcrvenazvezda.rs/terens-kinzi-u-crvenoj-zvezdi-28-12-2015.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Hapoel Jerusalem (2016–2018)===
On July 23, 2016, Kinsey signed a two-year deal with Israeli club [[Hapoel Jerusalem B.C.|Hapoel Jerusalem]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Tarence Kinsey arrives in Hapoel Jerusalem|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/featured/286482/tarence-kinsey-arrives-in-hapoel-jerusalem|access-date=July 23, 2016|work=Eurohoops.net|date=July 23, 2016}}</ref> In his first season with Jerusalem, Kinsey helped the team to win the [[2016 Israeli Basketball League Cup|2016 Israeli League Cup]] and [[2017 Israeli Basketball Super League Final Four|2017 Israeli League Championship]], as well as reaching the [[2016–17 EuroCup Basketball|2017 EuroCup Semifinals]].

===Breogán (2018)===
On September 1, 2018, Kinsey signed with [[CB Breogán|Cafés Candelas Breogán]] of the [[Liga ACB]] for the 2018–19 season.<ref>{{cite news |title=Breogan signs Tarence Kinsey |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/spain/acb/287305/breogan-signs-tarence-kinsey.html |access-date=September 1, 2018 |work=Sportando |date=September 1, 2018 }}{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

===Dijon (2018–2019)===
On December 3, 2018, Kinsey signed with [[JDA Dijon Basket|JDA Dijon]] of the [[LNB Pro A|Pro A]] for the rest of the 2018–19 season.<ref>{{cite news |title=UN GROS CV EN RENFORT : TARENCE KINSEY EST DIJONNAIS|url=https://www.jdadijon.com/2018/12/03/un-gros-cv-en-renfort-tarence-kinsey-est-dijonnais|access-date=December 3, 2018 |work=jdadijon.com |date=December 3, 2018}}</ref>

===Orlandina Basket (2019–present)===

On September 11, 2019, he has signed with [[Orlandina Basket]] of the [[Serie A2 Basket]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/capo-dorlando-sign-tarnce-kinsey/|title=Capo d'Orlando sign Tarence Kinsey|date=September 11, 2019|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=September 12, 2019|last1=Skerletic |first1=Dario }}</ref>
